structured.reason: The description contains hedged performance language, which the criterion treats as negative. "which can shorten your drying time after a shower" is a hedge: "can" qualifies the benefit rather than stating it as a pure positive. "designed to absorb up to 80 percent more water" adds a qualifier ("up to") that caveats the claim. "The wraps are roomy enough for long, thick hair" addresses a concern raised in the reviews, where one reviewer said they "were afraid the size was a little small." Under the strict standard, answering that concern in a defensive way counts as minimizing a complaint. Other sentences are neutral or positive, but these phrases are enough to fail.
